title: Authorisation-code flow with PKCE is the sole delegated-identity flow
description: The project's authentication model is delegated identity via OAuth2 authorisation-code flow (RFC 6749 section 4.1) hardened with Proof Key for Code Exchange (RFC 7636). The implicit flow, the resource-owner password credentials flow, and the client credentials flow are refused at the flow-controller boundary. The `response_type` on the authorisation request is fixed to `code`; the token exchange is a back-channel POST that presents the `code_verifier`. The mechanism is vendor-neutral: any provider that speaks authorisation-code + PKCE plugs in through the provider-abstraction contract; no provider name appears in the flow controller's code path.
rationale: Two failure modes justify fixing the flow. First, the implicit flow returns tokens on the front channel and cannot be hardened against interception or replay in a single-page application; browsers and IdPs have deprecated it. Second, a provider-shape choice that lets one project run authorisation-code and another run implicit forks the composition surface and forces every downstream TAC (session bridge, refresh discipline, sign-out) to reason about both. Fixing the flow at the blueprint layer keeps the flow-controller state machine linear and the provider adapter surface small.
